variable {V : Type*} [ORingStructure V] [V↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧* 𝗜𝚺₁]

private theorem read_put_other (file x : V) (p q : Fin 9) (h : p ≠ q) :
    regValue (put p x file) q = regValue file q := write_other file x p q h

/-- Every coordinate except TW and WS is retained by the complete file effect. -/
theorem paramPushFile_other (file : V) (i : Fin 9)
    (ht : i ≠ twReg) (hs : i ≠ wsReg) :
    regValue (paramPushFile file) i = regValue file i := by
  rw [paramPushFile, read_put_other _ _ twReg i ht.symm,
    read_put_other _ _ wsReg i hs.symm]

/-- The copy/restore tail permits arbitrary TW and needs only S1=0. -/
theorem copy_tail_run (file : V) (h1 : regValue file s1Reg = 0) :
    controlRun (7 * regValue file p1Reg + 2) (liveValue (number copyEntry : V) file) =
      liveValue (number exit : V) (put twReg (regValue file twReg + regValue file p1Reg) file) := by
  simpa only [show paramOccurrence.copy.test = copyEntry from rfl,
    show paramOccurrence.restore.exit = exit from rfl] using param_copy_run paramOccurrence file h1

/-- Actual275→301, with positive internal time and exact complete-file output. -/
theorem ax_param_push_run (file : V) (h1 : regValue file s1Reg = 0)
    (h2 : regValue file s2Reg = 0) :
    ∃ time : V, 1 ≤ time ∧ controlRun time (liveValue (number entry : V) file) =
      liveValue (number exit : V) (paramPushFile file) := by
  simpa only [show paramOccurrence.push.first.test = entry from rfl,
    show paramOccurrence.restore.exit = exit from rfl] using param_push_run paramOccurrence file h1 h2

end Model

text_by_sha256.8291ff2e547375d0b30acbe5c307b28bb17f0bf3:
A reusable occurrence emitter would reduce the repetitive source authoring. It
should emit instances of the existing MoveShape, CopyShape, PairShape,
PushShape, ParamPushShape, CopyBackShape and ConstructorShape interfaces. The
unbounded arithmetic proofs remain in their already checked modules. The
emitter is untrusted: each generated field is still a Lean proof about the
actual literal tree and catalogue.

The first version can be deliberately small. Give it a pinned source tree, a
macro kind, a concrete register assignment and an explicit list of catalogue
controls. It independently extracts each source instruction, its complete path
and each resolved target. Match the complete local control graph against a
fixed declarative macro pattern. Reject a mismatch; never infer correctness
from contiguous indices or a constant shift alone. In particular, inspect the
exit instruction separately: the two P1 pushes have identical executing
patterns, but their exits 248 and 301 begin different macros. The preserved
unexecuted correction in this directory demonstrates why that check matters.

Emit source, typed audit and literal inventory as one deterministic bundle.
Use the already passed `literal_target` helper for every successor, so the
proof does not evaluate `actualEntries.idxOf`. Import only the generic contract
needed for the occurrence. Keep the endpoint and full-file contract explicit,
including both scratch-zero premises and arbitrary internal clocks. Separate
shape instances from composition modules, so a composition only uses public
contracts and Cantor identities and does not elaborate the finite shapes again.
Metadata must distinguish the catalogue index from the represented live number
and a register-program control from a binary-machine state.

This first version saves authoring and review work; it does not by itself reduce
Lean evaluation cost. It should initially reproduce the existing selected
275–301 source/audit exactly, then reproduce the checked 222–248 and 248–275
interfaces with the appropriate boundary facts. Root can compare generated
bytes before authorizing any new proof run. No new emitter has been written or
executed in this task.

For compilation cost, a separate small experiment could factor each complete
`source q = (path, edge)` equality into one named fact per control, then use
those facts in all edge and target obligations. The target proof would rewrite
the source and destination pairs before its finite tree walk. This may avoid
repeated evaluation of `FiniteControlTable254.source`, whose definition indexes
the list `leafEntries ActualTree254.tree`; it requires an actual bounded
measurement before any speed claim. It neither changes that catalogue nor adds
proof-limit options. If a single late source-index fact itself exceeds default
limits, the next proof problem is a structural catalogue-index lemma through
the tree's left/right decomposition, not a larger recursion limit or unchecked
generated lookup table.

Keep one original template and one manifest of generated unit identities rather
than a separate compiler framework for every occurrence. Each actual source
and focused audit still gets its own fresh source-object binding before audit,
terminal record and existing 120-second shared limit. Reuse successful objects
only from actual PASS records. A future production manifest may group small
occurrences only after measurements establish headroom; no such grouping or
success is assumed here.

26-instruction pattern as the checked 222–248 occurrence, with every executing
control and successor index increased by 53. The next instruction itself is
different: control 301 begins an AC push and is `decnz 1`. The first unexecuted
draft copied the earlier exit's `decnz 2` statement; source review caught this,
and the exact draft plus the two corrected endpoint statements are preserved
under `history/draft1-before-exit-binding` and `exit-binding-repair.json`.

`ArithmeticControlAXNextParamPush254.lean` imports only the checked generic
ParamPush module. It uses the passed literal-target helper and repaired
`read_put_other` wrapper. With S1 = S2 = 0, it supplies positive internal time and
the exact file `TW := oldP1; WS := cantor(oldTW, oldWS)`, preserving the other
seven coordinates. The copy/restore tail 294–301 requires only S1 = 0, permits
arbitrary TW, and takes exactly `7 * oldP1 + 2` internal steps. The audit has six
named probes and eight typed clients. The source and audit remain uncompiled;
there is no guard or selected new object.

The complete literal-tree syntax/path comparison also identifies AC push
301–327 as the checked 136–162 pattern shifted by 165, and the zero-tag
constructor 327–354 as the checked 195–222 pattern shifted by 132. Those two
occurrences are not yet drafted here. They would let us compose 275–354 with
the exact output `TW := wim(oldP1, oldAC); WS := cantor(oldTW, oldWS)`, retaining
the other seven coordinates. This is the ordinary `par1F` then `f104` prefix of
`f75`/`f76` in L2Axioms254. That ordinary evaluator is a semantic guide; it is
not an imported internal-model execution theorem.

All source contracts quantify over arbitrary internal IΣ1 files and clocks.
The finite parser compares instructions and consumed paths, without executing
a register program or a Turing machine. The later complete AX branch,
interpreter/Enum equivalence and PA endpoint remain open.

text_by_sha256.b2f63418204b6acc73dd6dc322f564a5b0c02a47:
# Internal AX parameter push at controls 275–301

[ArithmeticControlAXNextParamPush254](../../Lean/BusyBeaver/ZFC/ArithmeticControlAXNextParamPush254.lean) proves the actual parameter1 push at **275→301**. For every internal register file in a model of IΣ₁, with S1=S2=0 initially, it supplies a positive internal execution time and the exact full-file effect:

- `TW := oldP1`;
- `WS := cantor(oldTW, oldWS)`;
- all other seven coordinates unchanged, including P1 and both scratch coordinates.

The copy/restore tail **294→301** has a separate exact-time contract: it takes `7 * oldP1 + 2` internal steps, requires only S1=0, permits arbitrary TW, and changes TW to `oldTW + oldP1` while retaining every other coordinate. The proof instantiates the checked [generic parameter-push contract](arithmetic_control_param_push254.md). Its finite occurrence binds 26 executing instruction edges and 34 successors; the unbounded execution comes from that generic theorem.

The [typed audit](arithmetic_control_ax_next_param_push254_audit.lean) contains six named axiom probes and eight callers, covering the entry/copy/exit bindings, arbitrary retained coordinates, both scratch coordinates, the tail and the full push. The first actual run passed in 63.345 seconds for source and 1.906 seconds for audit, with zero warnings. The three control facts use `propext`; the three file/execution reports use only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The [verification record](results/arithmetic-control-ax-next-param-push254-verification.json) retains exact commands, outputs and fresh-object captures before audit.

The [independent actual-evidence review](results/arithmetic-control-ax-next-param-push254-review.json) checks all 224 recorded inputs, the exact 98-project import closure, six cached Foundation/Mathlib pairs (five directly imported), and Init/Omega. Its separate source review independently decodes all 27 control bindings, including the exit, and the 34 successor paths from the full literal tree. The reviewer subsequently authored the publication builder; root-owned execution, installation and maintained preparation remain separate.

The first uncompiled draft copied the earlier occurrence's exit instruction `decnz 2`. The new exit, control 301, begins an AC push and is `decnz 1`. The theorem and typed caller were corrected, along with the following-block comment, before compilation. [The history](results/arithmetic-control-ax-next-param-push254-history.json) preserves that draft, its correction, the source-only inventory and reviews, preparation, actual source/audit PASS, raw logs and root receipts. No failed proof attempt for this module is claimed. Later continuation plans in that history remain plans.

The [provider proposal](results/arithmetic-control-ax-next-param-push254-provider-proposal.json) pins the generic ParamPush parent and its exact source/object pairs. That older parent recorded its source object before audit but did not save a separate fresh-first-provider field. The guard explicitly resolves its recorded `LEAN_PATH` now; it does not claim that this lookup was captured historically. This new unit records both the source object and its first provider before audit. Replay requires the exact cached providers; compiled caches are excluded, and no clean-checkout dependency rebuild is certified.

The maintained [guard](check_arithmetic_control_ax_next_param_push254.py) changes only its source, audit and provider-proposal default paths. Preparation performs no compiler or version query:

```sh
python3 -B Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/ZFC/check_arithmetic_control_ax_next_param_push254.py \
  --repo "$PWD" \
  --dependency-root /path/to/the/recorded/dependency-root \
  --param-push-evidence Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/ZFC/results/arithmetic-control-param-push254-verification.json \
  --output /tmp/fresh-ax-next-param-push-preparation \
  --prepare-only
```

Omitting `--prepare-only` in a fresh output directory runs source and audit under default proof limits, one thread, 4,096 MiB and a shared 120-second budget. This contract covers the stated push and its tail. The complete AX branch, interpreter/Enum comparison and internal binary consistency equivalence remain separate obligations.

The register program is Mira-Cult's, imported from Jeff's verification; the original TMBuilder framework is Wade's. [Prog254.lean](../../Lean/BusyBeaver/ZFC/Prog254.lean) records the source and attribution.
